chunks: And from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When Allah (Glorified is His Majesty) loves a servant, He chokes him with affliction with a choking, and causes trials to flow towards him copiously; so when He calls him, He says: 'I am here, My servant, I am here! If I were to hasten for you what you asked for, indeed I am able to do it; but if I have stored up for you, then what I have stored up for you is better for you.'
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah afflict those He loves with trials?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the divine wisdom behind afflictions (bala') for those whom Allah loves. It describes how Allah tests His beloved servants with intense trials, and when they call upon Him, He responds with a promise that while He could grant their immediate requests, the reward He has stored for them in the Hereafter is superior.

en.muhajir-b-ali: 39. It has been narrated that Abu Ja'far (a.s) said:

When Allah loves a person, He chokes him with afflictions until he is immersed in them completely and trials flow towards him copiously. Then when he calls out to Him, He (Allah) replies, 'I am here My servant, here I am! If I wished to hasten towards you what you are asking for, then indeed I am able to do it; but what I have amassed for you (for the hereafter) is better for you.'
